question: What is one significant drawback of the Green Revolution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Loss of biodiversity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution, which began in the mid-20th century, significantly increased agricultural productivity but led to the **loss of biodiversity** as it focused on monoculture farming.
 
• High-yielding varieties (HYVs) of crops like wheat and rice were heavily promoted, replacing traditional crop varieties and reducing **genetic diversity**.
 
• The extensive use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides further degraded ecosystems, harming **pollinators, insects, and soil microorganisms**.
 
• The reliance on a few crop species made agricultural systems more vulnerable to **diseases, pests, and climate change**, as genetic diversity acts as a natural buffer.
 
• Regions with rich agricultural traditions saw the **disappearance of indigenous crop varieties**, which were often better suited to local conditions and required fewer inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monoculture:** The practice of growing a single crop over a large area, which increases productivity but reduces biodiversity and makes crops more susceptible to pests and diseases.
 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYVs):** These are genetically improved crop varieties that produce more output per hectare but require significant inputs like water, fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• **Agrochemical Dependency:** The Green Revolution led to the intensive use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides, which caused soil degradation and water contamination.
 
• **Soil Health and Fertility:** Continuous monoculture and excessive chemical use diminished soil organic matter, leading to decreased fertility over time.
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture:** Practices like crop rotation, organic farming, and the use of traditional seeds are being promoted to counteract the negative impacts of the Green Revolution and restore biodiversity.
